Title: Jail Incarceration
Label: Jail Incarceration
Subtitle: Rate of residents admitted to local jails (not including prisons) per 100,000 adults ages 16 and older.
MethodsNote:
Jails hold a variety of people including those who are not granted or are unable to afford bail while awaiting trial, those serving sentences less than one year on a misdemeanor conviction, and those awaiting transfer to a state prison. Prisons are defined as New York State facilities where people serve sentences of more than a year on a felony conviction. 

Data analysis conducted in collaboration with NYC Center for Innovation through Data Intelligence (CIDI).

Approximately 30% of admissions were unable to be geocoded to a community district. As a result, the rates of incarceration are underestimated. 

Data have been de-duplicated by individual (based on NYSID). The data represent the number of unique people admitted to local jails at the community district, Borough, and NYC level. A person may be counted multiple times if they were admitted to jail on different occasions with addresses in different community districts. If a person was admitted to jail multiple times but with an address consistently in the same community district, they would be counted once. 29.5% of the total had more than one instance of incarceration while in the same CD of residence.  

These data define jail incarceration as the total admissions to jail and are not comparable to data from the 2015 CHPs, which defined jail incarceration based on average daily population.
DenominatorSource: NYC DOHMH population estimates, modified from US Census Bureau interpolated intercensal population estimates, 2016. Updated Sept 2017
